title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 1
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: A class of 18 pupils scored a mean of 62 on a test. A second class of 42 pupils scored a mean of 74. What is the mean score across both classes?
questions.explanation: Total marks are 18×62 + 42×74 = 4224, over 60 pupils, giving 70.4. The unweighted average of 62 and 74 is 68.0, which is wrong because the larger class scored higher.

questions.prompt: A price of £240.00 rises by 25% and the new price is then reduced by 20%. What is the final price?
questions.explanation: £240.00 × 1.25 = £300.00, then × 0.80 = £240.00. The percentages do not add: a 25% rise followed by a 20% fall returns exactly to the start, because 1.25 × 0.8 = 1.

questions.prompt: One machine can complete a job in 4 hours and another in 6 hours. Working together at those rates, how long do they take?
questions.explanation: Rates add, not times: 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 of the job per hour, so the job takes 12/5 = 2.4 hours. Averaging the two times to get 5 hours is the standard error.

questions.prompt: In a club the ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 5. When 12 more girls join, the ratio becomes 3 : 7. How many members were in the club originally?
questions.explanation: Write the original numbers as 3k and 5k. After the change, 3k : (5k + 12) = 3 : 7, so 7(3k) = 3(5k + 12), giving 21k = 15k + 36, so k = 6. The original total is 8k = 48.

questions.prompt: £4,000.00 is invested at 5% a year, compounded annually. What is it worth after 3 years, to the nearest penny?
questions.explanation: £4,000.00 × 1.05³ = £4,630.50. Simple interest would give £4,600.00; the difference is the interest earned on interest.

questions.prompt: A driver covers 120 miles at 40 mph and returns over the same 120 miles at 60 mph. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: Time out is 120/40 = 3 hours and back is 120/60 = 2 hours, so 240 miles take 5 hours: 48 mph. The average of 40 and 60 is 50, which is wrong because more time is spent at the slower speed.

questions.prompt: If 40% of a number is 64, what is 75% of the same number?
questions.explanation: 0.40x = 64 gives x = 64/0.4 = 160. Then 0.75 × 160 = 120. Working out the whole first is the reliable route; scaling 64 by 75/40 reaches the same place.

questions.prompt: Three adult tickets and two child tickets cost £34.50. Two adult tickets and five child tickets cost £36.00. What is the price of one adult ticket?
A bag holds 5 red and 7 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.explanation: P(first red) = 5/12. After removing one red, P(second red) = 4/11. Multiplying gives 15.2%. Treating the draws as independent would give 17.4%.

questions.prompt: A room measures 4.5 m by 6.2 m. Flooring costs £27.50 per square metre. What is the cost of covering the floor?
questions.explanation: Area is 4.5 × 6.2 = 27.90 m². At £27.50 per m² that is £767.25.

questions.prompt: After a 14% reduction, a coat costs £258.00. What was the price before the reduction?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 86% of the original, so the original is £258.00 / 0.86 = £300.00. Adding 14% to the sale price gives £294.12, which is the common mistake — the percentage applies to the larger figure.

questions.prompt: 3 litres of a 20% solution are mixed with 5 litres of a 60% solution. What is the concentration of the mixture?
questions.explanation: Solute is 3×0.20 + 5×0.60 = 3.6 litres in 8 litres of mixture: 45.0%. The midpoint of 20 and 60 is 40%, which ignores the larger volume of the stronger solution.

questions.prompt: A sequence starts at 7 and increases by 5 each term. What is the 24th term?
questions.explanation: The kth term is 7 + (k − 1) × 5. For k = 24: 7 + 23 × 5 = 122. Using k rather than k − 1 gives 127.

questions.prompt: An item costing £60.00 is sold for £80.00. What is the profit margin as a percentage of the selling price?
questions.explanation: Profit is £20.00. As a share of the selling price that is 20/80 = 25.0%. As a share of cost it would be 33.3% — margin and markup are different measures of the same profit.

questions.prompt: Of 120 people surveyed, 74 read the local paper, 58 listen to local radio and 12 do neither. How many do both?
questions.explanation: 120 − 12 = 108 do at least one. By inclusion and exclusion, both = 74 + 58 − 108 = 24.

questions.prompt: A van travels 12.4 km on each litre of fuel. How far can it travel on 45 litres?
questions.explanation: Distance is fuel multiplied by consumption: 45 × 12.4 = 558.0 km. Dividing instead of multiplying is the error the distractors are built around.

questions.prompt: Six values are recorded: 12, 14, 15, 15, 19, 96. By how much does the mean exceed the median?
questions.explanation: Mean is 171/6 = 28.50; median is the average of the third and fourth values, 15. The difference is 13.5, driven by the single large value.

questions.prompt: A machine listed at £850.00 is sold with a 15% discount, and 20% tax is then added to the discounted price. What does the buyer pay?
questions.explanation: £850.00 × 0.85 = £722.50, then × 1.20 = £867.00. Netting the percentages to +5% gives £892.50 and is wrong.

questions.prompt: 6 workers complete a task in 15 days. Working at the same rate, how long would 10 workers take?
questions.explanation: The total work is 6 × 15 = 90 worker-days. Divided among 10 workers that is 9 days. More workers means fewer days, so the answer must be below 15.

questions.prompt: A market share rises from 8% to 10%. By what percentage has the share increased?
questions.explanation: The rise is 2 percentage points, but as a percentage of the original share it is 2/8 = 25%. Reporting 2% conflates a percentage point with a percentage.

questions.prompt: Option A charges £0.42 a mile with no standing charge. Option B charges £90.00 plus £0.18 a mile. For a journey of 500 miles, which is cheaper and by how much?
questions.explanation: Option A costs £210.00; Option B costs £90.00 + £90.00 = £180.00. Option B is cheaper by £30.00. The two are equal at 375 miles, above which the standing charge is worth paying.
